messages:
Renee Ortiz: Heads-up — we need a compact battlecard and a one-slide bench callout for next week's webinar. Goal: 3 repeatable claims + 3 one-line rebuttals vs Cloud APIs / infra vendors. Keep copy punchy for SDRs.

Noah Park: Sounds good. Propose the three claims be: predictable tail latency (SLO-backed), cost controls via batching/cache, and migration-free model swaps across deployments. Short and repeatable.

Samir Dutta: I'll add a micro-benchmark paragraph and a tiny failover example. Quick numbers from perf lab: simulated region outage -> smart routing -> compatible variant preserved ~91% throughput and added ~170-200ms median latency depending on model. Will note test conditions.

Renee Ortiz: Perfect. Can you write the PR-ready bench blurb and a 10s salesperson hook for each claim? SDRs will read those on cold outreach.

Samir Dutta: Micro-bench blurb (draft): "Benchmark summary: In controlled cross-region failover tests, Redwood Inference maintained ~91% of baseline throughput while incurring a median latency increase of ~+185ms when routing to a compatible variant (8k sequence tests, median of 6 runs). Results vary by model and payload; the key outcome is graceful degradation rather than full outage."

Noah Park: Love it. 10s hooks: 
- Predictable latency: "SLO-backed tail-latency guarantees + automatic fallbacks."
- Cost controls: "Smart batching & prefix caching reduce per-token spend without extra infra work."
- Migration-free: "Same API across Hosted, Dedicated, Private 1 so you can swap models without code changes.

CopyBot: Reminder: Please add alt-text for the bench chart image: "Chart: throughput retention and median latency during simulated cross-region failover showing ~91% throughput retention and +185ms median latency increase."

Renee Ortiz: Rebuttals (short): 
- To Cloud APIs: "We give SLA-aware fallbacks and transparent routing so your app doesn't go dark when one region or provider is impaired."
- To infra vendors: "We own runtime tuning and rollouts so your infra team can focus on capacity, not kernel selection."
- To DIY self-host: "Avoid the ops cliff: we handle quantization, KV cache, and production batching best practices.

Noah Park: For the webinar landing A/B lines, testing two variants: 
A) "Same API. Predictable performance. Flexible deployment."
B) "Keep features live during incidents 1 SLOs + smart routing."
Recommend tagging inbound leads by which headline they clicked and routing ops-sensitive leads to solutions.

Samir Dutta: Attached a tiny flow snippet for the slide: 
``
outage -> smart routing -> compatible variant -> median latency +185ms, throughput ~91%
```
I'll export as PNG with alt text.

LaunchBot: Event reminder: launch-battlecard-review scheduled tomorrow 2:00pm PT. Invite shared with #marketing and #sales.

Renee Ortiz: Thanks all. Final asks before I lock: (1) vote on headline A vs B in the doc, (2) confirm micro-bench blurb wording. If green I'll tag Design for the flow visual and mark battlecard field-ready after review.

Noah Park: Voting A for PLG focus, B for technical buyer streams. Lean A for webinar hero.

Samir Dutta: Micro-bench blurb confirmed. Exporting chart + alt text now.

Renee Ortiz: Great. I'll consolidate and post final in #marketing-assets. If the review goes well, we'll ship the webinar registration and battlecard to sales.
